output.brief: The Kestria buffering is most likely caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not the CDN move. Smart-TV 5.2 users are at about 5.9% rebuffering, while web, iOS/Android and older smart-TV users on the same Tessaline CDN and the same ISPs stay at 0.6–0.7%. The CDN switch and the handball launch do not explain that split: the stalls began on 9 Oct, the same day 5.2 went live, two days before handball. Confidence is moderate-to-high, but the telemetry is an ad hoc query and the 5.2 link to cancellations is not established; the price rise also explains part of the churn. Next: have engineering roll back 5.2 adaptive-streaming settings for Kestria (or pause the 5.2 rollout) and confirm the fix in the data. Do not send the SLA notice, withhold fees, or move traffic back on this evidence. Do not mute the rebuffering alert. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard as a fast follow-up, even though the pipeline rebuild is about six weeks out.
output.methodChoice: EDF analysis using initial evidence plus X6 (client/app/ISP breakdown) as the discriminating item; X1 and other items not collected.
